title: The Huasteca Potosina in October: Weather, Rivers, and What to Expect
metaTitle: Huasteca Potosina in October 2026: Weather & Rivers
metaDescription: Huasteca Potosina in October: the end of the rainy season, waterfalls at full flow, what to pack, and which tours to book. A 2026 guide with real prices.
excerpt: October is the bridge between the rainy and dry seasons in the Huasteca Potosina: rivers at their peak, waterfalls at full power, and Xantolo just around the corner.
contentHtml:
October in the Huasteca Potosina is the transition month between the rainy season and the dry season. The rivers reach their highest flow, the waterfalls are at full power, and temperatures range from 22 °C to 32 °C. Many travelers wonder whether it's worth visiting the region at this time of year, assuming the rain will ruin the trip. The reality is different: October offers scenery you won't see in any other month. Visiting the Huasteca Potosina in October means seeing Tamul Waterfall (Cascada de Tamul) as a 105-meter curtain of water at full strength, running the Tampaón River at a level that makes rafting more thrilling, and arriving just as towns prepare for Xantolo, the Huasteca's Day of the Dead festival.

This guide covers everything you need to know about Huasteca weather in October, the state of the rivers and waterfalls, updated 2026 prices, and the practical tips we use with the groups we coordinate every season. According to the local operators we work with, October rain is concentrated in the first half of the month, and the second half is noticeably clearer, which makes late October an excellent window for a trip.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators across the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: September 2026. If you already have your dates set, check out our all-inclusive packages to visit the Huasteca Potosina in October.

Huasteca weather in October: what really happens, month by month

What is the weather like in the Huasteca Potosina in October?

Huasteca weather in October means afternoon showers concentrated in the first half of the month, usually between 2:00 and 6:00 PM, and clear mornings that let you start tours without a hitch. The average high in October is 32 °C, and the overnight low drops to 20 °C, so nights are noticeably cooler than in July or August. Relative humidity stays high, around 80%, so light, quick-dry clothing is a must.

The groups we coordinate this time of year always head out before 9:00 AM to make the most of the hours when rain is least likely. On most days, by the time the tour gets back to the meeting point, the afternoon rain has already passed or is just starting. Planning your itinerary from higher to lower elevation also helps: lowland jungle areas, like the banks of the Tampaón, get less daily rainfall than the high slopes around Xilitla. End of the rainy season in the Huasteca: when exactly does it end?

The rainy season in the Huasteca winds down gradually between the last week of October and mid-November. There's no single exact date: in La Niña years, the rains drag on into the first week of November; in neutral years, the second half of October is already mostly dry. For 2026, historical patterns suggest that from October 18 to 31 conditions will be favorable on most days.

This matters if you plan to visit Puente de Dios in Tamasopo, where the wooden access walkway can close temporarily when heavy rain pushes the river too high. Read our complete guide to Puente de Dios in Tamasopo for month-by-month access conditions.

Waterfalls in October: rivers at their peak and a one-of-a-kind water show

Tamul Waterfall and the boat trip in October

Seeing the waterfalls in October is an experience with no equivalent in the dry months. Tamul Waterfall, with its 105-meter drop over the Tampaón River, practically doubles its volume of water compared with March or April. The boat trip from the Tanchachín dock covers about 7 kilometers round trip and takes 2 to 2.5 hours. Access to the site includes admission and a shared boat; our Tamul Expedition includes it for $1,550 MXN per person, with transportation from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles, breakfast, a NOM-09 certified guide, and admission fees.

The travelers we coordinate in October all agree on one thing: the morning mist that forms over the Tampaón River before 10:00 AM creates a sight that dry-season visitors never get to see. The green of the riverside vegetation is at its most intense, and the sounds of the jungle (birds, water, and wind) are part of the experience. Read the definitive guide to visiting Tamul Waterfall for all the logistics before you book.

Tamasopo and Minas Viejas waterfalls: water levels and access in October

The Tamasopo Waterfalls (Cascadas de Tamasopo) are probably the most accessible in the region in October, with paved roads up to the entrance and trails that stay open even during light rain. Admission is $60 MXN per person in 2026. October's flow makes the site's three main drops look connected in a single continuous curtain, something that practically never happens in February. Arrive before 10:00 AM to beat the peak crowds, which are heaviest between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM on weekends.

The Minas Viejas Waterfalls, on the other hand, require a hike of about 45 minutes, with some dirt stretches that get slippery after recent rain. Boots or sneakers with good grip are essential in October. See our complete guide to the Minas Viejas Waterfalls for trail conditions by season. How much does it cost to visit the Huasteca Potosina in October? 2026 price breakdown

Visiting the Huasteca Potosina in October is very affordable compared with the high season in December or Holy Week (Semana Santa). The tours we sell range from $900 MXN to $1,950 MXN per person; the Tamul Expedition, with transportation, breakfast, admission fees, and a certified guide, costs $1,550 MXN. Individual admission fees vary: Puente de Dios costs $150 MXN and the Tamasopo Waterfalls $60 MXN. Rafting on the Tampaón River, with transportation and lunch included, costs $1,950 MXN per person and runs from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Kids ages 6 to 10 pay about 70% of the adult price; children under 6 pay 50%.

For stays with lodging, packages for two start at $8,699 MXN, with a hotel in Xilitla and tours included. Read our article on how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026 for a full breakdown by type of traveler.

Practical tips for visiting the Huasteca Potosina in October

Packing and planning your logistics the right way makes the difference between a smooth trip and one full of surprises. These are the tips we give every group we coordinate during the end of the rainy season, based on real experience week after week.

  • Book at least 48 hours ahead: All tours depart every day of the year, but free cancellation only applies with 48 hours' notice. If the weather suddenly turns, you'll have room to reschedule at no cost.
  • Bring quick-dry clothes and a full-coverage rain layer: Humidity tops 80% in October. Damp cotton causes chafing on long hikes. Check our packing checklist for the Potosí jungle so you don't forget anything essential.
  • Pick the second half of October if you want more sun: From October 18 to 31, the chance of clear days goes up considerably, especially in the low river areas like the Tampaón and Tamul.
  • Wear shoes with grip for the trails: The paths to Minas Viejas, Xilitla, and some smaller waterfalls get muddy in the days after it rains. Trail sneakers or light waterproof boots are the best option for these routes, not river sandals.
  • Budget cash for small expenses: Many local access points (rural parking lots, food vendors along the way, tips for local guides) don't take cards. Bring at least $500 MXN in cash per person per day, on top of the cost of the tour.
  • Catch Xantolo if you travel in the last week: From October 28 to 31, Huasteca towns start preparing for Xantolo with altars, dances, and markets full of cempasúchil (Mexican marigold) flowers. It's a cultural bonus no other month offers. Read our guide to Xantolo in the Huasteca Potosina to plan the cultural visit alongside your nature tours.

Suggested itinerary for the Huasteca Potosina in October: 3 days

The groups we host in October usually have 3 to 5 days available. A well-planned 3-day itinerary covers the most iconic spots without rushing, while working around the month's typical weather. The most practical home base is Ciudad Valles, from which you can reach most of the main attractions in under 2 hours. According to local operators, many October visitors choose 3-night packages based in Ciudad Valles or Tamasopo.

Days 1 and 2: Waterfalls, rivers, and the high jungle

The first day is built around the most physically demanding attractions: Tamul Waterfall by boat, the Minas Viejas Waterfall, or Las Pozas in Xilitla. Leave Ciudad Valles at 8:00 AM and get back before 5:00 PM to avoid the afternoon rain on the roads home. The second day is for Tamasopo: Puente de Dios ($150 MXN admission) and the Tamasopo Waterfalls ($60 MXN), which is exactly what our Water Route does if you choose Tamasopo as the second stop: $1,600 MXN per person, with transportation and admission fees. Rafting on the Tampaón River ($1,950 MXN per person, with transportation and lunch) takes 7 hours and needs a day of its own. Check out the available Huasteca Potosina tours in October and mix and match them at your own pace.

Day 3: Tamtoc Archaeological Site

The third day is ideal for experiences with less time in the water: the Tamtoc Archaeological Site (for now it only opens on Sundays, from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, so plan your trip to be there that day), which works well even after recent rain because its plazas drain quickly. If you're traveling in the last week of the month, add a stop at a local Xantolo market. See our 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary guide for versions tailored to families or couples.

Frequently asked questions about the Huasteca Potosina in October

Are the waterfalls open all through October, or do they close because of rain?

Most attractions stay open all October. The Tamasopo Waterfalls have reliable access. Puente de Dios may close temporarily (between 1 and 3 days a month) when heavy rain raises the river. We recommend confirming with the local operator the day before.

How much does a full tour in the Huasteca Potosina cost in October 2026?

The tours we sell range from $900 MXN to $1,950 MXN per person; the Tamul Expedition costs $1,550 MXN, with transportation, breakfast, admission fees, and a NOM-09 certified guide. Packages with a hotel for two start at $8,699 MXN. Rafting on the Tampaón River costs $1,950 MXN per person with transportation and lunch. Kids ages 6 to 10 pay 70% of the adult price.

Is it better to visit in the first or second half of October?

The second half, from October 18 to 31, has more clear days and lines up with the start of Xantolo in Huastec towns. The first half has more afternoon rain, but also waterfalls with higher flow. Both work if you plan to head out before 9:00 AM every day.

Is the Huasteca Potosina safe to visit in October with family or as a couple?

Yes. Huasteca weather in October follows predictable patterns: short afternoon showers and clear mornings. For families, the Tamasopo Waterfalls are a calm place to swim. For couples, the boat trip to Tamul and Las Pozas in Xilitla are the top picks. Always go with a NOM-09 certified guide for river activities.
